worked_examples.title: Worked Problem: Calculating RNI, Doubling Time & Dependency Ratio
worked_examples.problem: A country has a total population of 100 million, with 42 million aged 0–14, 54 million aged 15–64, and 4 million aged 65+. Its Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is 32 per 1,000 and Crude Death Rate (CDR) is 7 per 1,000 (assuming zero net migration). Calculate: (a) Rate of Natural Increase (RNI), (b) Doubling Time, and (c) Age Dependency Ratio (ADR).
worked_examples.step_solution:
1. RNI = (CBR - CDR) / 10 = (32 - 7) / 10 = 25 / 10 = 2.5% per year.
2. Doubling Time = 70 / RNI = 70 / 2.5 = 28 years.
3. ADR = [(Young 0-14 + Old 65+) / Working 15-64] × 100 = [(42 + 4) / 54] × 100 = (46 / 54) × 100 ≈ 85.2 dependents per 100 working-age people.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Never forget to divide (CBR - CDR) by 10 when converting per-1,000 rates into percentages!

worked_examples.title: Worked Problem: Calculating RNI, Doubling Time & Dependency Ratio
worked_examples.problem: A country has a total population of 100 million, with 42 million aged 0–14, 54 million aged 15–64, and 4 million aged 65+. Its Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is 32 per 1,000 and Crude Death Rate (CDR) is 7 per 1,000 (assuming zero net migration). Calculate: (a) Rate of Natural Increase (RNI), (b) Doubling Time, and (c) Age Dependency Ratio (ADR).
worked_examples.step_solution:
1. RNI = (CBR - CDR) / 10 = (32 - 7) / 10 = 25 / 10 = 2.5% per year.
2. Doubling Time = 70 / RNI = 70 / 2.5 = 28 years.
3. ADR = [(Young 0-14 + Old 65+) / Working 15-64] × 100 = [(42 + 4) / 54] × 100 = (46 / 54) × 100 ≈ 85.2 dependents per 100 working-age people.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Never forget to divide (CBR - CDR) by 10 when converting per-1,000 rates into percentages!

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Population geography links demographic dynamics with resource sustainability. Balancing population growth with human capital investment, family planning, and sustainable watershed governance drives socio-economic transformation.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Balancing economic growth, social equity, and environmental stewardship; circular economy and renewable resource thresholds.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **RNI is expressed as a percentage**: RNI is expressed as a percentage: RNI (%) = (Crude Birth Rate - Crude Death Rate) / 10.
- **Population Doubling Time (in years) is approximated by the Rule of 70**: Population Doubling Time (in years) is approximated by the Rule of 70: Doubling Time = 70 / Growth Rate (%).
- **Key Principle**: A broad-based triangular population pyramid indicates a young population with high birth rates and high youth dependency.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Demographic Transition Curve: Stage 1 (High BR & DR) ──> Stage 2 (DR drops, rapid growth) ──> Stage 3 (BR drops) ──> Stage 4 (Low BR & DR, stable population).
```

Ethiopia's demographic structure features a large youth cohort, offering a potential "Demographic Dividend" as investments in secondary/higher education and industrial parks expand.

worked_examples.title: Worked Problem: Calculating RNI, Doubling Time & Dependency Ratio
worked_examples.problem: A country has a total population of 100 million, with 42 million aged 0–14, 54 million aged 15–64, and 4 million aged 65+. Its Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is 32 per 1,000 and Crude Death Rate (CDR) is 7 per 1,000 (assuming zero net migration). Calculate: (a) Rate of Natural Increase (RNI), (b) Doubling Time, and (c) Age Dependency Ratio (ADR).
worked_examples.step_solution:
1. RNI = (CBR - CDR) / 10 = (32 - 7) / 10 = 25 / 10 = 2.5% per year.
2. Doubling Time = 70 / RNI = 70 / 2.5 = 28 years.
3. ADR = [(Young 0-14 + Old 65+) / Working 15-64] × 100 = [(42 + 4) / 54] × 100 = (46 / 54) × 100 ≈ 85.2 dependents per 100 working-age people.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Never forget to divide (CBR - CDR) by 10 when converting per-1,000 rates into percentages!
